notes: TBox delete of a stored rule, as geography-delete-0005: Linux is Unix-like in every world; w1 has its separator stored by name, w2 reached it only through the rule. The relative path (q1) is written with the system's separator (a firm rule over a relation). Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30. q3 ('the same character as web URLs') is a join over named individuals; the URL separator is its bridge (firm). Relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check. q1 is labelled fol since then (it builds a path string); Z3 checks it first and this file's find is a second check.

fol.notes: Systems are an uninterpreted sort; uses_path_separator is read as a function to an enumeration of separators (the question compares 'the same character', one per system), so different separators are distinct. As the DL file: Linux is Unix-like in every world; w1 has its separator stored by name, w2 reaches it only through the deleted rule. The URL separator is a stored bridge no world touches. q1 (the relative path, a string built from the separator character) is labelled fol since 2026-10-31, as its replace mirror: the path is a String (rel_path, local) built by a firm rule from the separator's character (sep_char, local); the DL file's find over a named path individual stays as a second check.
